subject: ventures/gutter-guard-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a gutter installation shop who bids leaf-guard retrofits (screen, foam, helmet, micromesh) and tracks job margin

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateBid on 3 scenarios (default 140 ft screen ranch; 220 ft 2-story micromesh with clean-first, 16 ft fascia, 2 extra downspouts, 12 miters, occupied; 180 ft 2-story reverse-curve, steep, occupied, proposed $2000) and recomputed each by hand-built formula in a separate Python script from the page's default rates: totals 2.7 h / $566.43 cost / $786.71 price ($5.62/ft); 15.28 h / $3313.08 / $4601.50 ($20.92/ft); 7.70 h / $1818.77 / $2526.07, margin of $2000 = 9.06%. All matched to the cent. Also checked page claims: $36 x 1.32 = $47.52; 4.4 clean-first hours on 220 ft; mesh/screen price ratio 3.02x on the same 140 ft run (page says three or four times). Margin-on-price formula cost/(1-m) is the textbook gross-margin form. Limit: the Python check used the same documented formula, not another vendor's tool, and no published trade price book was compared.
evidence.completeness: README features checked: included ranch run with extra stories/feet/miters (works), extra downspouts, clean-first, fascia, steep roof, occupied hours (all in calc.mjs and exercised), walk-away price and proposed-price comparison (works, 9.06% margin case above), Copy bid summary (formatBidSummary, tested), job-type presets that do not overwrite typed rates (suggestedJobHours, tested), local usage tally with opt-out (usage.mjs + footer control), plus shipped extras: printable proposal (proposal.mjs), share links (share.mjs), 3 comparison pages and a pricing walkthrough, all present with tests. No stubs or TODOs found. VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype and all three hypotheses are untested; no real shop has used it.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/gutter-guard-bid-calculator && node --test *.test.mjs: 150 tests, 150 pass, 0 fail, about 0.5 s. Three hand-seeded mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (tree clean afterwards): (1) price = totalCost/(1+margin) instead of /(1-margin): 3 failures; (2) extraMiters subtracts one more than included: 4 failures; (3) clean-first hours use extraFeet instead of whole run: 3 failures. All caught. Gap: tests were not run in a real browser, index.html wiring is checked by string/regex tests (page.test.mjs).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs, usage.mjs, parts of index.html, share.mjs and proposal.mjs. Pure calc module with no DOM, input validation that throws on non-numeric, negative and 100% margin, frozen presets, tidy exports. Defects: every rate input defaults to 0 via ?? 0, so a caller omitting hoursPerExtraStory silently prices the story at zero rather than erroring (the UI always supplies values, so low); alias variable billableExtraDownspouts is a no-op copy; includedMiters/includedDownspouts rules are asymmetric (downspouts cannot be below 1 but the extra count is trusted separately, so downspoutCount is informational only); hour/rate tables are duplicated between JOB presets, suggestedJobHours and index.html default attributes, so they can drift.
evidence.claims: Checked: free, no build, no network (grep of index.html, share.mjs, usage.mjs finds only localStorage, no fetch/XHR); wages omitted from the copied summary (formatBidSummary prints no cost or wage lines); disclaimer present in README, index.html footer, comparison pages and the proposal text; usage events listed in README match usage.mjs; FAQ numbers (1.5 h/$2.25, 1.7/$3.40, 2.1/$6.25, 2.4/$8.50, 0.35 h per 10 ft, 1.2 h per story, $8 kit, $22 adapter) match calc.mjs and the form defaults. Not backed: the market premises ($8/ft leaf-filter special, Home Depot DIY micromesh price) are uncited, and starting hours are stated as ballpark. Link defects: llms.txt points at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of marisstella.app; sitemap.xml and robots.txt Sitemap use relative URLs, which the sitemap protocol does not accept.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a shop enters 140 ft, 1 story, 4 miters, gets $786.71 ($5.62/ft) with walk-away $566.43; switches to the mesh colonial preset and gets $4601.50; types a competitor price and sees margin or loss; copies a customer-safe summary or prints a proposal with deposit and hold days. A shop owner can finish a bid in minutes, but must replace the starting hours and coil costs with their own, and the tool gives no way to save multiple jobs or rate sets beyond one local bid.
evidence.domain: Cost-plus bidding with burdened labor, overhead on direct cost and margin on price is the standard small-contractor method and is applied correctly. Departures a senior installer would flag: no material waste or overage factor and no material markup; no sales tax on materials; labor is crew-hours at a single wage with no crew-size or productivity-by-pitch model; extra-story and steep-roof are flat hours not scaled by footage; starting hours and costs are unsourced guesses (README says so); no gutter-guard-specific scope such as removing old guards, re-pitching or hanger spacing. Fine for a first-cut sanity check, not a full estimating method.

defects.what: No material waste/overage factor, material markup or sales tax, so the walk-away price understates true cost on real jobs
Starting hours and coil costs are unsourced ballpark figures; no calibration against any real crew or supplier price list
llms.txt links all point at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of marisstella.app
sitemap.xml and the robots.txt Sitemap line use relative URLs, which crawlers ignore
Omitted rate inputs silently default to zero in calculateBid instead of throwing
Dead alias billableExtraDownspouts and informational-only downspoutCount

verdict: Arithmetic is right and well tested: three scenarios recomputed to the cent, 150 of 150 tests pass, and three seeded bugs (margin formula, miter include, clean-first basis) were each caught. Code is clean, claims about privacy, disclaimer and FAQ figures check out, and the tool covers a real bidding job end to end. It meets the bar, narrowly: domain is 2 because the method omits waste, markup and tax and the hour and cost defaults are unsourced guesses, and no real shop has used it (hypotheses untested, stage prototype). The stale github.io links in llms.txt and relative sitemap URLs are the concrete fixable defects.
